name: Charyn Canyon
description: A dramatic red-rock canyon about 150 m deep. The most famous part, the Valley of Castles, is a 3 km walk between eroded sandstone towers down to the Charyn River. Often compared to a small Grand Canyon.
howToGet: About 3–3.5 hours by car east of Almaty. No regular public bus goes to the viewpoint: take a group day tour, hire a car with a driver or rent a car.
season: April–June and September–October are best. Summer is very hot in the canyon; winter is possible but cold and windy.
durationHint: Full day from Almaty (often combined with Kolsai and Kaindy on a 2-day trip)

prices.label: Group day tour from Almaty (per person)

name: Kolsai Lakes
region: Kolsay Lakes National Park, Raiymbek District
description: A chain of three alpine lakes surrounded by spruce forest in the Northern Tien Shan. The lower lake is easy to reach; a trail of about 8 km leads to the middle lake. Guesthouses are available in Saty village.
howToGet: About 5–6 hours by car from Almaty via Saty village. Usually visited on a 2–3 day tour together with Kaindy Lake and Charyn Canyon.
season: June–September is best. Mountain roads and trails can be closed or icy from November to April.

prices.label: 2-day group tour from Almaty (Kolsai + Kaindy + Charyn)

name: Kaindy Lake
region: Kolsay Lakes National Park, near Saty village
description: A lake formed by a 1911 earthquake landslide. Trunks of drowned spruce trees still rise out of the turquoise water, creating a famous 'sunken forest'.
howToGet: From Saty village the last 12 km are a rough dirt road: locals offer 4x4 transfers or you can hike/ride a horse. Usually combined with Kolsai Lakes.
season: June–September. In winter the lake freezes and access is difficult.

name: Medeu
description: A legendary high-altitude outdoor skating rink at 1,691 m in a mountain valley above Almaty. Nearby is the Medeu dam with a long staircase and great views.
howToGet: City bus No. 12 from Dostyk Avenue (about 30–40 min) or a taxi (about 20–30 min) from the city centre.
season: Skating: roughly November–March. In summer the valley is popular for walks and events.

name: Shymbulak
description: The largest ski resort in Central Asia, reached by a gondola from Medeu. Cable cars continue up to Talgar Pass (about 3,200 m) with views of glaciers and peaks. In summer it is a hiking and viewpoint destination.
howToGet: Go to Medeu (bus No. 12 or taxi), then take the gondola up to Shymbulak and further chairlifts to Talgar Pass.
season: Skiing: about December–April. Summer (June–September) for views and hiking.

prices.label: Gondola Medeu – Shymbulak – Talgar Pass, return (adult)

name: Big Almaty Lake
region: Ile-Alatau National Park, south of Almaty
description: A turquoise mountain lake at about 2,500 m, surrounded by high peaks. It is a protected water reservoir for the city, so swimming is not allowed.
howToGet: About 1–1.5 hours by taxi or car via the Big Almaty Gorge road. The last part of the road may be closed to private cars; check the current rules before you go.
season: June–October is best; the water colour is most vivid in summer. Road access can be limited in winter and spring.

name: Kok-Tobe Hill
description: A hill on the edge of the city centre with panoramic views of Almaty and the mountains, the TV tower, a small amusement park, cafés and the famous Beatles monument. Especially beautiful at sunset.
howToGet: Cable car from the lower station near the Palace of the Republic (Dostyk Ave / Abai Ave), or by taxi/shuttle to the top.

name: Panfilov Park and Ascension Cathedral
description: A large green park in the centre of Almaty with the colourful wooden Ascension Cathedral (built 1907 without nails, survived the 1911 earthquake), a war memorial and an eternal flame.
howToGet: Walk from the city centre or take the metro to Zhibek Zholy station (about 10 minutes walk).

name: Green Bazaar
description: Almaty's most famous market. Try dried fruits, nuts, honey, kurt, horse-meat delicacies, Korean salads and local sweets. A great place to feel everyday local life.
howToGet: A short walk from Panfilov Park, or metro to Zhibek Zholy station.
season: All year; it is usually closed on Mondays (check before visiting).

name: Central State Museum of Kazakhstan
description: One of the largest museums in Central Asia, covering Kazakh history from ancient times, nomadic culture, ethnography and modern history.
howToGet: Located near Republic Square on Samal-1 district; reachable by bus or taxi from the centre.
season: All year; usually closed on one weekday (check opening hours).

name: Altyn-Emel National Park (Singing Dune)
description: A vast desert park with the Singing Dune that hums in dry windy weather, the colourful Aktau 'chalk' mountains, Besshatyr burial mounds and wild kulans and gazelles.
howToGet: About 4 hours by car from Almaty. A permit from the park office in Basshi village is required; most visitors go with a tour or a 4x4 with a driver.
season: April–June and September–October. Summer is extremely hot.

name: Tamgaly Petroglyphs
description: A UNESCO World Heritage site with about 5,000 Bronze Age rock carvings, including the famous sun-headed deities, in a quiet gorge of the Chu-Ili mountains.
howToGet: About 2.5–3 hours by car north-west of Almaty. No public transport; go by car, taxi or tour.
season: April–October. Avoid midday heat in summer.

name: Turgen Gorge and Waterfalls
description: A green mountain gorge with several waterfalls (Bear, Kairak, Bozzhyra), a trout farm and horse riding. The road continues up to the Assy Plateau.
howToGet: About 1.5 hours by car east of Almaty via Turgen village. Taxi or tour recommended.
season: May–October is best. Waterfalls freeze in winter (ice climbing).

name: Assy Plateau
description: A wide high-mountain pasture at about 2,500 m where nomadic herders still keep yurts and horses in summer. Home to the Assy-Turgen astronomical observatory.
howToGet: Through Turgen Gorge on a rough mountain road; a 4x4 or a tour is strongly recommended.

name: Issyk Lake and Issyk Kurgan Museum
description: The Issyk Kurgan is where the 'Golden Man' — a Saka warrior in golden armour, a national symbol of Kazakhstan — was found. The open-air museum is in Esik town; the mountain lake Issyk is about 15 km higher up the gorge.
howToGet: About 1–1.5 hours by car or suburban bus from Almaty to Esik, then taxi to the lake.
season: Museum all year; the lake is best May–October.

name: Butakovka Gorge and Waterfall
description: A popular easy hiking gorge close to the city with a forest trail to a small waterfall. Good for a first acclimatisation walk.
howToGet: About 30 minutes by taxi from the centre to the start of the trail in Butakovka village.

name: Kapshagay Reservoir (Qonaev)
description: A large reservoir on the Ili River known as the 'beach of Almaty': sandy beaches, resorts, water sports and summer cottages.
howToGet: About 1–1.5 hours by car or intercity bus/minibus from Almaty to Qonaev.

name: First President's Park
description: A large landscaped park with fountains, lawns and alleys, with the mountains as a backdrop. Popular for evening walks and photos.
howToGet: By taxi or bus to Al-Farabi Avenue / Navoi Street.
season: All year; best from April to October.
